cleanIntro: The ZEROED 22 is a take-apart rimfire can, and CMMG says so plainly: it is completely user serviceable and comes fully apart for cleaning. One book covers all three versions. The 22 is the full-size can, 5.5 inches with 8 baffles. The 22 K is the short can, 4.5 inches with 6 baffles. The 22 Plus ships full-size with the shorter K tube in the box, so you can build it either way. It is .22 LR rated for full auto, .17 HMR and 22 MAG semi-auto only, and threads straight onto a 1/2-28 barrel, hand tight. The routine lane takes it off the host and cleans the outside. The deep lane is CMMG's full teardown, which the book asks for every 500 to 1000 rounds: front cap off, baffle stack out, mount off, clean, and rebuild with the baffle marks lined up.

steps.title: ⛔ Host unloaded and the ACTION OPEN before the can comes off
steps.action: Make the host firearm safe first: unloaded, with the action OPEN so you can see it is clear. CMMG asks for the action open every time the ZEROED 22 goes on or comes off. How to unload your pistol or rifle is in that gun's own manual.
steps.prose: Your hand is about to be at the muzzle. An open action is how you know nothing is in the chamber while it is.
steps.quote: Make sure firearm is unloaded and the action is open to verify clear before removing your suppressor from the host firearm.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Removal, printed p.6

steps.title: ⛔ Let it COOL, or wear gloves
steps.action: Let the suppressor cool to room temperature before you take it off or work on it. If it has to come off hot, wear protective gloves.
steps.prose: A small aluminum can gets hot fast on a rimfire string, and it does not look hot.
steps.quote: Allow suppressor to cool to ambient temperature before removal and/or service. If suppressor must be removed or installed while hot, protective gloves should be worn.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Safety notices, printed p.5

steps.title: Know the rating: 1/2-28 direct thread, .22 LR full auto
steps.action: The ZEROED 22 threads directly onto a 1/2-28 barrel with a square, 90-degree shoulder. CMMG rates all three versions for .22 LR in full auto, and for .17 HMR and 22 MAG in semi-auto only.
steps.prose: Check the host against this before the can goes back on, not after. The mount has to seat flat on that shoulder.
steps.caution: Regularly check that the suppressor is securely threaded onto the barrel between strings of fire.
steps.quote: The ZEROED 22 is designed to attach directly to 1/2-28” threaded barrels with a 90-degree shoulder.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Installation, printed p.5

steps.title: Off the host: grip at the MOUNT, counter-clockwise
steps.action: Grip the lower part of the suppressor firmly, around the mount, and turn it counter-clockwise to unthread it from the barrel.
steps.prose: Grip at the mount, not out at the front cap. Turning the can by the cap can loosen the cap on the tube instead of the mount on the barrel.
steps.quote: Firmly grip the lower portion of the suppressor around the mount and turn counterclockwise to unthread.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Removal, printed p.6

steps.title: Field strip complete: off the host
steps.action: With the can off the host, routine care is the outside: solvent and a nylon brush on the tube and front cap, and clean mount threads before it goes back on. The full teardown is the deep clean, and CMMG wants it every 500 to 1000 rounds.
steps.prose: Carbon builds up fast in a rimfire can. Leave it too long and the baffles lock together.
steps.quote: The ZEROED 22 is user serviceable and can be fully taken apart for thorough cleaning.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Maintenance, printed p.6

deepSteps.title: Front cap off: hold the tube, turn the cap counter-clockwise
deepSteps.action: Grip the suppressor tube firmly in one hand and turn the front cap counter-clockwise to remove it. If carbon has it stuck, put a 1/4-inch Allen wrench, or a 1/4-inch hex bit and driver, into the hex opening in the front cap to help turn it.
deepSteps.prose: The hex in the cap is there for exactly this. Use it before you reach for pliers on an aluminum cap.
deepSteps.aside: If Necessary: A 1/4” Allen wrench or 1/4” hex bit and driver can be inserted into the front cap opening to assist in removal.
deepSteps.quote: Firmly grip the tube of suppressor in one hand and turn the front cap counterclockwise to remove.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Disassembly, printed p.6

deepSteps.title: Baffle stack out: turn the can upside down
deepSteps.action: Turn the suppressor upside down carefully so the baffle stack slides out of the tube, and set it aside. The baffles should pull apart from each other. If carbon has locked them, tap the baffle edges gently.
deepSteps.prose: Gently means gently. These are the parts the bullet passes through, and a bent edge is a baffle strike.
deepSteps.aside: Baffles should pull apart from one another, gently tap the baffle edges if carbon locked.
deepSteps.quote: Carefully turn the suppressor upside down to remove the baffle stack from the tube and set aside.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Disassembly, printed p.6

deepSteps.title: Stack stuck? A small WOODEN dowel through the mount
deepSteps.action: If the baffle stack will not slide out of the tube, put a small wooden dowel rod in through the rear of the mount and push the stack out gently.
deepSteps.prose: Wood, not a metal rod or a screwdriver. CMMG wrote GENTLY in capitals.
deepSteps.quote: If the baffle stack does not slide out of the tube, a small wooden dowel rod can be inserted through the rear of the mount to GENTLY push the baffle stack out.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Disassembly, printed p.6

deepSteps.title: Mount off the tube: counter-clockwise. The O-rings stay on
deepSteps.action: To take the mount off the tube, twist the mount counter-clockwise to unthread it. Leave the O-rings on the front cap and the rear mount where they are: CMMG says they do not need to come off for regular disassembly and cleaning.
deepSteps.prose: The mount is the serialized part, so keep track of it.
deepSteps.caution: O-rings on the front cap and rear mount (018 Viton), do not need to be removed for regular disassembly and cleaning.
deepSteps.quote: To remove the suppressor mount from the tube, twist the mount counterclockwise to unthread.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Disassembly, printed p.6

deepSteps.title: Clean: solvent and nylon brush. Ultrasonic for STEEL parts only
deepSteps.action: Clean the inside and outside with a quality gun cleaning solvent and a nylon brush. The steel parts, the baffles and the rear mount, can go in an ultrasonic cleaner, but take care not to damage the phosphate finish on the mount. Do NOT put the aluminum tube or front cap in an ultrasonic cleaner.
deepSteps.prose: Steel baffles, aluminum tube and cap. That split decides what goes in the ultrasonic.
deepSteps.aside: Steel parts such as the baffles and rear mount can be ultrasonically cleaned, though caution should be taken not to damage the phosphate finish on the mount.
deepSteps.quote: A quality gun cleaning solvent and nylon brush can be used to clean interior and exterior portions of the suppressor.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Cleaning, printed p.7
deepSteps.warn: Ultrasonic cleaners should NOT be used to clean the tube or front cap.

deepSteps.title: Before it goes back: clean threads, light oil, anti-seize
deepSteps.action: Make sure every part surface and thread is clean. Put a light coat of oil on the mount surfaces, and a thin coat of anti-seize on the threads of the mount and the front cap.
deepSteps.prose: Aluminum threads into a steel mount. The anti-seize is what stops galling, so the can comes apart again next time.
deepSteps.quote: Ensure all part surfaces and threads are clean. Lightly oil mount surfaces and apply a thin coat of anti-seize to the threads of the mount and front cap to prevent galling or seizing.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Reassembly, printed p.7

deepSteps.title: 22 Plus: pick the configuration. Full-size 5.5" with all baffles, K 4.5" with 6
deepSteps.action: On a 22 Plus, choose the build now. Full size uses the longer 5.5-inch tube and all of the baffles. The K configuration uses the shorter 4.5-inch tube with 6 baffles; store the leftover baffles and tube somewhere safe and secure. A ZEROED 22 or a 22 K has one tube and goes back with all of its own baffles.
deepSteps.prose: The tube length and the baffle count have to match. Count the baffles before the stack goes in.
deepSteps.aside: For K-configuration, use the shorter 4.5” tube with 6 baffles and store the remaining baffles and tube in a safe and secure location.
deepSteps.quote: NOTE: For 22 Plus full size configuration use the longer 5.5” tube and all baffles.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Reassembly, printed p.7

deepSteps.title: Front cap onto the tube first
deepSteps.action: Thread the front cap onto the outer tube. The stack goes in from the other end.
deepSteps.prose: Cap first means the stack has something to sit against when you slide it in.
deepSteps.quote: Install front cap on the outer tube.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Reassembly, printed p.7

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Stack the baffles with the INDEX MARKS LINED UP
deepSteps.action: The baffles are all the same and can go in any order. Stack them together and make sure the index marks on their edges line up, then slide the stack carefully into the tube.
deepSteps.prose: Any order, but not any rotation. The marks are what CMMG gives you to get the rebuild right.
deepSteps.aside: Carefully slide the baffle stack into the suppressor tube.
deepSteps.quote: Baffles are identical and can be stacked in any order. Stack baffles together and ensure marks on the other edge are aligned.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Reassembly, printed p.7

deepSteps.title: Mount into the tube: clockwise, no cross-threading
deepSteps.action: Thread the mount into the tube by turning it clockwise, and take care not to cross-thread it.
deepSteps.prose: If it does not start smoothly, back it out and start again. Do not force it.
deepSteps.quote: Thread the mount into the suppressor tube by turning clockwise. Take care not to cross-thread.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 22 | 22K | 22 Plus — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Reassembly, printed p.7

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & MOUNT THREADS
tasks: Gun cleaning solvent and a nylon brush on the outside of the tube and front cap.
Clean the mount threads before the can goes back on.
Full teardown every 500–1000 rounds; sooner with dirtier ammunition.

cleaning.name: BAFFLES & MOUNT (STEEL)
tasks: Solvent and a nylon brush, inside and out.
May go in an ultrasonic cleaner; protect the mount's phosphate finish.
Leave the O-rings on the mount; they do not need to come off.

cleaning.name: TUBE & FRONT CAP (ALUMINUM)
tasks: Solvent and a nylon brush, inside and out.
Do not put the tube or front cap in an ultrasonic cleaner.

cleaning.name: BEFORE REASSEMBLY
tasks: All part surfaces and threads clean.
A light coat of oil on the mount surfaces.
A thin coat of anti-seize on the mount and front cap threads.
22 Plus: 5.5" tube with all baffles, or 4.5" tube with 6.

reassembly: All part surfaces and threads clean; a light coat of oil on the mount surfaces and a thin coat of anti-seize on the mount and front cap threads.
22 Plus only: the 5.5" tube with all baffles for full size, or the 4.5" tube with 6 baffles for K, with the spare baffles and tube stored safely.
Front cap onto the outer tube.
Baffles stacked together in any order, with the index marks on their edges lined up; slide the stack carefully into the tube.
Mount threaded into the tube clockwise, taking care not to cross-thread.
Host firearm unloaded, with the action open to verify clear.
Line the mount's threaded opening up with the barrel threads and screw the can on, by hand only, without cross-threading.
The mount seats completely against the barrel's shoulder face.
fncheck: With the host unloaded and the action open: the can is on by hand only and the mount sits completely against the barrel's shoulder face, with no gap. The front cap and the mount are both threaded fully home on the tube. Check that the can is still threaded on securely between strings of fire, with the gun unloaded and gloves on, because it may be hot.
